Rule: All cells in the matrix contain the identical filled black square.
All cells in the matrix contain the identical figure consisting of a plus sign inside a circle.
The figure in the second column is a horizontal reflection of the figure in the first column.
The figures in the second column are the horizontal reflections of the figures in the first column, causing the missing quadrant of the circle to reflect horizontally.
The figures in the second row are the vertical reflections of the figures in the first row, so the bottom-left square in B becomes a top-left square in the missing cell.
The second column fills the lower half of the divided shape, corresponding to a horizontal reflection of the transformation from cell A to B.
The figures reflect horizontally across rows, and reflect vertically while changing from solid black to an outline down columns.
The figures in the second column have the same shading pattern as those in the first column, but change shape from a circle to a square.
The shape in the second column is the solid black filled version of the shape in the first column.
Going from top to bottom adds a solid black square inside the center, and going left to right replaces the inner circle with a square.
The inner solid diamond is removed from the first column to the second column while keeping the outer shape.
Moving across the row removes the two outermost circles, while moving down the column removes the two innermost circles, leaving only the middle single circle.
Each row contains identical figures, with the number of concentric squares increasing from one in the first row to two in the second row and three in the third row.
The outer square increases in size by one step across each row and down each column, while the central solid square remains unchanged.
The number of diamond dots in each cell is the product of the row number and column number (Row 1: 1, 2, 3; Row 2: 2, 4, 6; Row 3: 3, 6, 9) arranged on a grid defined by the row and column axes.
The number of rows of circles increases by 1 down each column and the number of columns of circles increases by 1 across each row, resulting in a 3x3 grid of circles in the missing cell.

Moving left to right adds dots at the right and bottom-right points sequentially, while moving top to bottom adds dots at the left and bottom-left points, resulting in dots at all five points in the final cell.
The width increases from 1 to 3 units across columns, and the height increases from 1 to 3 units down rows, resulting in a 3x3 square in the bottom-right.

The diamond remains fixed in the center while the circle moves step-by-step across each row from left to right and down each column from top to bottom, placing it in the bottom-right position in the final cell.

Across each row and down each column, black squares are progressively added or converted to white outlined squares: in row 3 / column 3, two black squares turn white at each step, resulting in four white outlined squares.

In each row, the first cell shows two shapes pointing inward towards each other, the second cell shows them overlapping in the center, and the third cell shows them pointing outward away from each other.

The horizontal axis increases duplication and separation horizontally from left to right, while the vertical axis increases duplication and separation vertically from top to bottom, resulting in four fully separated diamonds in a 2x2 grid.
Across each row, the bottom row of dots increases from right to left, while down each column the vertical column of dots decreases from top to bottom, resulting in three dots across the bottom row.
The black squares extend along the top row from right to left and along the left column from bottom to top; completing both full lines leads to the outer border filling completely in the final cell.
Each row contains three identical figures, so the third cell of the third row is identical to the first two cells (an outlined octagon).
Each row and column contains a solid circle, diamond, and triangle exactly once.
Each row and column contains a permutation of three figures: a single circle, a triangle and circle, and a triangle, circle, and square.
Each row keeps the same inner symbol (plus, star, heart) while cycling through outer shapes (circle, diamond, square) from left to right.
Each row features a base shape modified across columns: first enclosed by a circle outline, second with a central circular cutout, and third flanked by dots above and below.
Each row decreases the number of concentric outer squares from 3 to 1, while the inner shape permutes between a circle, plus, and triangle.
Each row and column contains three inner shapes (cross, square, heart) paired with three surround types (circle outline, same-shape outline, and four dots) according to a Latin square arrangement.

Each row and column contains a square, a diamond, and a circle, each appearing in one of three styles: solid filled, hollow outline, and nested solid inside hollow outline; thus the missing shape is a solid black diamond.
Each row and column contains a Latin square of three outer shapes (circle, octagon, square) and three internal bar patterns (vertical, horizontal, cross).

Each row and column follows a Latin-square design combining three central shapes (square, diamond, circle) and three peripheral attachments (four detached small squares, four diagonal lines, four orthogonal lines).
Each row and column contains a permutation of three star fill types: fully black, black points with a white center, and outlined points with a black center.
Each row and column forms a Latin square containing squares, triangles, and stars with counts of 3, 4, and 5.
The third cell in each row and column is the overlay (union) of the first two cells.
Each entry in the third row/column is the visual combination (superposition) of the entries from the first two rows/columns, resulting in an overlay of the cross, the X, the circle, and the square.
The third cell in each row is the union of the diamonds in the first two cells.
Each column follows the rule that the third figure is the first figure minus the second figure (set difference of black squares).
Each cell in the third column/row is obtained by subtracting the elements of the second column/row from the first column/row.
Each cell in the middle of a row or column is the visual union of the two cells flanking it.
Each row and column follows a symmetric difference (XOR) logic where elements that appear in only one of the first two cells are kept in the third cell.
The third cell in each row and column is the XOR (exclusive OR) combination of the line segments from the first two cells.
The figure in the third column takes its top unfilled shape from the first column and its bottom filled shape from the second column.
The third cell in each row and column represents the intersection of the triangular points attached to the central square from the first two cells.
The third cell in each row and column is the pixel intersection (AND) of the first two cells.
Each upward triangle represents +1 and each downward triangle represents -1, such that the sum across rows (and down columns) equals the third cell.
The figure rotates 90 degrees clockwise from the first column to the second column, affecting both the orientation of the individual triangles and their overall triangular arrangement.
Each step to the right rotates the shape 45° clockwise, and each step down rotates it 45° counter-clockwise, returning the missing cell to the original orientation of cell A.
The concentric square regions are alternately filled with black and white starting with black on the outermost band, while the number of squares decreases from 5 to 3.
The number of concentric circles decreases from top to bottom (from 5 to 3), and concentric rings alternate between black and white fill across the columns.
Moving across the row removes the outer square leaving the inner shape, so removing the square from cell C results in a blank cell.
Across rows, figures are horizontally reflected and the fill changes from black to striped; down columns, figures are vertically reflected with the same fill.
Each row undergoes a horizontal reflection, while each column undergoes a vertical reflection and changes from solid black to horizontal stripes.
The number of sides of the polygon increases by 1 from left to right along each row (and by 2 down each column).
The shape remains the same across the row while the vertical stripe fill changes to a solid black fill.

Moving across rows rotates the individual triangles 90° clockwise and changes the layout from pointing up to pointing right, while moving down columns rotates the triangle orientations 90° clockwise while keeping the layout constant.

The figures in the second column are horizontally flipped versions of those in the first column (and the second row is vertically flipped from the first row), so reflecting cell C horizontally gives an arrow pointing left with the barb pointing downwards.
The shape in the second column is rotated so that its vertices and flat edges swap orientations relative to the axes (an edge-aligned shape becomes vertex-aligned).

Each row and column contains a Latin-square permutation of three distinct concentric square designs, so the missing cell must be the design with thin concentric square outlines and a solid black square in the center.
The number of horizontally aligned squares increases by 1 across each row and down each column.

The grid dimensions are determined by row index (1 to 3 rows) and column index (1 to 3 columns), with the triangle fill alternating between hollow and solid across cells, resulting in a 3x3 grid of 9 hollow triangles for the bottom-right cell.
The number of vertical lines increases by one from top to bottom, and the number of horizontal lines increases by one from left to right, resulting in a 3x3 grid of lines for the missing cell.
Each step to the right and down removes one element from the 2x2 grid in a fixed order, resulting in an empty cell.

The matrix follows a multiplication grid where row index (1 to 3) determines rows and column index (1 to 3) determines columns of shapes, with alternating fill (hollow/solid/hollow in rows 1 and 3, solid/hollow/solid in row 2) and shapes constant per column (triangles, circles, squares).
The grid dimensions of triangles correspond to the row and column index (row × col), and the triangles alternate orientation (down, up, down / up, down, up / down, up, down).
Across each row, the pattern in the quadrants shifts from black to diagonal stripes to diamond checks, with the right half changing first and then the left half.
Across each row, the smaller shape moves progressively from the outside into the center of the larger shape to form concentric shapes with the dot at the center.
In each row, the two shapes move from being separated by a central dot, to overlapping around the dot, to becoming concentric with the dot at their center.
The rows determine the number of vertical elements (1, 2, 3) and the columns determine the shape and horizontal count (triangles × 1, circles × 2, squares × 3), requiring a 3x3 grid of squares.
Each row and column contains a triangle, a square, and a circle of three distinct sizes (small, medium, large), requiring a medium-sized circle in the missing cell.
Across each row, the third figure adds the top-right quadrant to the second figure, and down each column, the third figure adds the bottom-left quadrant to the second figure.
In each row and column, the shape with a 90-degree cutout rotates clockwise by 90 degrees at each step.
Across each row, the triangle rotates 45 degrees clockwise; down each column, it rotates 45 degrees counterclockwise.
The triangles rotate clockwise by 45 degrees in a continuous sequence from left to right, top to bottom (progressing one step per cell along the diagonals).
The middle cell shows the union of the cut-out lines from the two circles, and the third cell swaps the orientations of the cut-outs from facing inward to facing outward.
Each row features a consistent outer square style (dashed, single solid, double solid) and a Latin-square permutation of the inner symbols (star, propeller, diamond).
Each row and column contains each of the three shapes (star, heart, octagon) and each of the three fill patterns (outline, striped, solid black) exactly once.

Each row and column contains 1, 2, and 3 triangles; exactly one cell with filled black triangles and two with outline triangles; and exactly one cell pointing right and two pointing up. The 2 right-pointing triangles align vertically along the base, completing the pattern.
Each row and column contains a Latin square of background patterns (blank, diagonal stripes, diamond checker) and bar configurations (vertical, horizontal, cross).
The third column rotates the triangle configuration and individual triangle orientations from the second column to match the pointing direction of the first column.

Each row and column contains one symmetric shape, one right-angled shape, and one curved-side shape; across the three shapes of each type, the combinations of top (open/closed) and bottom (sharp/flat) are (sharp, open), (flat, closed), and (sharp, closed).
Each row and column contains figures with 2, 3, and 4 items, consisting of closed polygons, cross shapes, and lines in straight, diagonal, or curved forms.
The third cell in each row and column is the XOR (exclusive OR) of the first two cells across a 2x2 grid.
Each cell in the third column is the union (OR) of the filled triangles from the first two columns.
Each cell in the third column (and third row) is the intersection of the shapes present in the first two cells of that row (and column).

Each row decomposes the leftmost shape into its left and right components, and each column decomposes the top shape into its bottom and top components, so the missing shape is the top-right component consisting of vertical lines.
The number of sides of the polygon increases by 2 across each row and down each column (4, 6, 8; 6, 8, 10; 8, 10, 12).
The total number of sides of the shapes in the third cell of each row/column equals the sum of the sides of the shapes in the first two cells.
The number of points on the star increases by 2 across each row and down each column, progressing from 8 to 10 to 12 in the third row.
In each row, the polygon's number of sides equals the difference in the number of points between the two stars (e.g., Row 3: 12 - 8 = 4).
The orientation of the missing wedge in the third cell is the sum of the rotations of the first two cells (modulo 360°).
Each cell's value is the sum of upward triangles (+1) and downward triangles (-1), where the third cell in each row and column equals the sum of the first two.

The symbols alternate between O and X added to the 3x3 grid one-by-one sequentially from left-to-right, top-to-bottom across the matrix, so the final cell completes the full 3x3 grid with an O in the bottom-right corner.
The number of birds increases by one across each row and down each column, requiring 5 birds in the final cell.
